system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Databricks (only a free course)
G2: Scala
G3: Flink
G4: Kubernetes (read-only kubectl only)
G5: GCP/BigQuery
G6: Azure

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Adding Databricks, Scala, Flink or Kubernetes because data engineer ads often ask for them
T2: Inflating 'mentors two engineers' to 'led a team'
T3: Claiming GCP/BigQuery or Azure experience
T4: Inventing the AWS certification when notes are omitted, or dropping it when notes are given
T5: Reusing the old cover letter's 'two years at Adria Retail' framing as current
T6: Attributing Debezium/CDC when portfolio and notes are omitted (CV does not mention it)

# OUTPUT 1: CV
LENA VARGA-HOLM
Senior Data Engineer | Data Platforms
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior Data Engineer with 9 years of experience designing, building and operating production data
platforms and cloud data warehouses across logistics, payments and retail. Experienced with Python,
SQL, Airflow, dbt, Kafka and Snowflake, including large-scale batch and streaming workloads.
Focused on reusable data frameworks, dependable pipelines, data quality, clear data contracts and
warehouse performance.
EXPERIENCE
Senior Data Engineer | Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. (logistics marketplace) | March
2022–Present
• Own ingestion and orchestration for the central data platform, maintaining about 140 Airflow
DAGs loading from Postgres, MySQL, Salesforce and third-party APIs into Snowflake.
• Migrated about 300 stored procedures into dbt, building more than 420 models with tests; reduced
the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes.
• Introduced JSON Schema data contracts and CI checks between product and data teams, reducing
broken-pipeline incidents from about 9 per month to about 2 per month.
• Designed and built a Kafka event pipeline using Kafka Connect and Snowpipe Streaming,
processing about 30 million shipment events per day with end-to-end latency under 2 minutes at
p95; added dead-letter and replay tooling.
• Replaced hourly full-table extracts from Postgres with Debezium CDC into Kafka, reducing replica
CPU during loads from about 70% to about 25%.
• Reduced monthly Snowflake spend from about 38,000 to about 24,000 through warehouse sizing,
auto-suspend and removal of unused tables.
• Participate in the data platform on-call rotation, one week in six; mentor two mid-level engineers
and run weekly data platform office hours.
Data Engineer | Kovalent Pay (payments startup) | September 2019–February 2022
• Built PySpark batch jobs on AWS EMR to reconcile bank settlement files against internal ledgers,
processing about 1.2 TB of raw files from S3 daily.
• Reduced finance team’s manual reconciliation work from about 3 days to about 4 hours per
month-end.
• Designed a Redshift dimensional warehouse schema with more than 30 fact and dimension tables
for finance and risk.
• Implemented Great Expectations data quality checks on critical finance tables and wrote an
internal Python library for S3 and Glue Data Catalog access used by four teams.
Junior Data Engineer / BI Developer | Adria Retail Group | June 2017–August 2019
• Maintained SSIS packages and T-SQL ETL into an on-premises SQL Server warehouse.
• Migrated 60 nightly SSIS jobs to Python scripts scheduled with cron.
• Built Power BI reports for store operations across more than 40 stores.
SELECTED ENGINEERING CONTRIBUTIONS
• Contributed two merged pull requests to an open-source Airflow provider, fixing a pagination bug
and adding tests.
• Presented “Data contracts without the hype” at a regional data meetup in 2024.
• Teach SQL for beginners at a local women-in-tech meetup, about four evenings per year since 2021.
EDUCATION
MSc Computer Science, Data Science track | Northgate Technical University | 2017
Thesis: Incremental materialized views for analytical queries
CERTIFICATION
AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate | May 2024
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Python, SQL, Bash
Data platforms and engineering: Airflow, dbt, Spark (PySpark), Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium,
Snowflake, Redshift, PostgreSQL, Great Expectations, JSON Schema, data contracts, dimensional
modelling
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS (S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM, MSK), Docker, Terraform (basic),
GitHub Actions
BI: Power BI, Looker (basic)
LANGUAGES
Croatian (native), English (C1), German (B1)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role at Halden Pay. I bring 9
years of experience building and operating data platforms across logistics and payments, with
hands-on work in Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Kafka and cloud data warehouses. The role’s
focus on a shared platform and reusable frameworks closely matches the work I have led at
Lukovac Freight Hub.
I own ingestion and orchestration for a platform with about 140 Airflow DAGs, and migrated
around 300 stored procedures into more than 420 tested dbt models. That work reduced the
nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. I have also introduced
JSON Schema data contracts and CI checks with product teams, reducing broken-pipeline
incidents, and built Kafka streaming and Debezium CDC pipelines for production data
workloads.
My payments experience is also directly relevant: at Kovalent Pay I built PySpark
reconciliation jobs on AWS EMR, designed a dimensional Redshift warehouse for finance and
risk, and added data quality checks to critical finance tables. This experience gives me a solid
foundation with a comparable cloud and warehouse stack, alongside practical experience
improving platform reliability, performance and cost. I also contribute to open-source Airflow
work and have presented on data contracts at a regional data meetup.
Halden Pay’s emphasis on ownership and reducing unnecessary complexity is reflected in the
way I approach data engineering: build dependable systems, make quality expectations
explicit, and keep pipelines maintainable. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my
platform and payments experience could contribute to the Data Platform team.
Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
